title: Staffing in stages: the first team, then new teams
moduleTitle: Shared: Growing and managing a team
audience: Owners who plan to hire, train and supervise a cleaning team as demand grows.
learningOutcomes: Set a demand trigger for each hiring stage, linked to the break-even figure
Describe an induction gate that must be passed before unsupervised work
Explain what a team lead must be able to do before a second team starts

instruction.heading: Why staffing follows demand
instruction.body: The sample plan describes staffing in stages. The first week of jobs is done by a team, new employees are hired as contracts increase, and a new team is trained only once enough demand exists. The logic is sound. Hiring ahead of demand adds wages before revenue arrives, and hiring behind demand loses jobs and strains the people already working. Move one stage at a time, and let a measure you can see trigger each move.

instruction.heading: Setting triggers
instruction.body: A trigger is a level of demand that justifies the next hire. Derive it from the break-even work in the previous lesson. For example, a trigger might be a set number of booked hours per week, held for a set number of weeks, with a cash reserve in place. Write the trigger as a number and a rule, such as 'booked hours above a set level for three consecutive weeks'. The exact figure depends on your own costs and local market, so set it for your business and review it. Do not copy a figure from another business or from a sample document.

instruction.heading: The induction gate
instruction.body: The sample plan trains new employees on cleaning methods first, then on teamwork and professionalism. Turn that sequence into a gate. A new team member does not work unsupervised until they have completed induction on methods, workplace safety, chemicals, customer conduct and reporting, and a supervisor has signed off each task they are allowed to perform. The gate protects the client and the worker, and it creates a record.

instruction.heading: Teams work better when roles are clear
instruction.body: The sample plan prefers teams because they are more efficient, and it notes that some clients want a single cleaner instead. A team needs defined roles: a lead who checks the scope and the standard, workers who carry out the tasks, and a handover at the end of each visit. Team training is training in those roles, in the order the work is done, and in how to raise a problem quickly.

instruction.heading: Building a second team
instruction.body: A second team is built around a proven lead, not around a headcount. Before the second team starts, the lead should have run full jobs without supervision, be able to complete the scope checks, and be able to take a new person through the induction gate. Copy the induction, the scope and the standards, not the people. Keep the first team as the reference point, and check the second team's first five jobs against the same standards.

instruction.heading: Turnover and retention
instruction.body: The sample plan names employee turnover as a threat. Turnover has causes you can change: pay, rostering, the quality of induction, supervision, feedback and whether the work is valued. Pay and conditions must follow the award or agreement that applies to each worker.

instruction.heading: Employee or contractor
instruction.body: Whether a worker is an employee or a contractor affects pay, superannuation, insurance, tax and how much control you have over the work. The sample plan does not address this. Decide the classification by examining the actual working arrangement, not the label alone, and record your reasons.

procedure: Write the trigger for the next hire as a number and a rule, using the break-even figure.
Write the induction gate, listing each topic and the sign-off required.
Define the roles for each team: lead, worker and handover.
Confirm that the proposed lead has run full jobs without supervision before a new team starts.
Hire one stage at a time, and record which trigger was met and when.
Track turnover each month, with the reason for each leaver.
Check pay and classification against the applicable instrument before any offer is made.

workedExamples.situation: A sole owner has two regular bookings a week and a third booking has been requested for next month. The owner has one part-time helper who has finished induction but has not yet worked as a lead.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the owner hire a new team member now, and what must be in place before the third booking is accepted?
workedExamples.reasoning: The trigger has not been met, because one requested booking is not a sustained level of demand. The owner checks the helper against the induction gate and lets the helper lead the third booking under supervision. If demand holds for the full trigger period, the owner starts recruiting, with the induction gate ready before the first shift.

commonErrors.error: Hiring because the owner feels overloaded
commonErrors.prevention: Hire only when the written trigger has been met for the set period.

commonErrors.error: Starting a new team with no proven lead
commonErrors.prevention: Require the lead to complete full jobs without supervision and sign off the scope checks.

commonErrors.error: Letting new staff work unsupervised before induction is signed off
commonErrors.prevention: Use the induction gate and record each sign-off.
Check the working arrangement and record the reasons.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Under model WHS laws adopted in each state and territory, a business has duties to its workers, including information, training, instruction and supervision.
Where clients include schools, aged care or other services involving children or vulnerable people, state or territory screening requirements may apply to staff.
Check with the Fair Work Ombudsman or a qualified adviser.

qualityStandard: Each hire is supported by a written trigger that was met for the set period.
Every new worker has a dated induction record and a sign-off for each task they perform.
A new team starts only after its lead has been confirmed against the lead criteria.
Pay and classification have been checked against the applicable instrument, and the check is recorded.
documentationEvidence: Staffing plan with triggers and the dates they were met
Induction records and task sign-offs for each worker
summary: Staff in stages, and let a written trigger drive each stage.
The induction gate comes before any unsupervised work.
A second team needs a proven lead, not just more people.
Check pay, classification and screening rules before any offer is made.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should trigger the hiring of the next team member?
options: The owner feels overloaded and has been working late for a whole month
A competitor has just hired staff and the team is worried about it
The end of the financial year and the accountant has asked for a plan
A written demand trigger met for the set period, with the induction gate ready

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a new worker's first jobs be supervised?
options: To confirm methods, safety and customer conduct before the worker works unsupervised
To check that the owner is paid and that the bank has cleared it and the tax is paid
Because clients must be told about every shift and the client signs for each one
To avoid writing induction records and to skip the first week of pay for the staff

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the main purpose of a competency record for each team member?
options: Marketing the business to new customers each season and promoting it on the radio
Calculating the break-even point and the cost of the van and the phone each month
Showing which tasks each person has been checked to perform safely and to standard
Replacing the induction gate and the training for the whole crew each year
